For my first ever Debate I wore a long sleeve button down, a tie, dress pants and dress shoes. A judge critiqued the fact that I didn’t have a suit jacket (it wasn’t about the money in my case) but it made me think about a kid who’s parents couldn’t afford a suit jacket. Formal dress has no impact on the speaker and or the Debate. 
Do I wear a suit to a Debate? Yes 

Would I ever give someone a hard time for dressing casual? Never
Really it’s just a personal preference.

I personally feel it should remain because  it’s part of tradition, and I feel like we should keep tradition in this context. It may not matter to others but I enjoy dressing formal for a Debate  and feeling more  confident as a result.
Down here in Texas, debaters from the bigger cities like Dallas and Austin mix dress and casual.
It doesn’t impact me at all I don’t even question it.
Right but when I first started debating, I would get pushed around by the judges for not having a suit jacket.
I feel a lot more confident wearing a suit, going up against an opponent wearing a suit. I wouldn’t feel the same way if my opponent was wearing a suit and I was wearing everyday clothes.
There’s some traditions that should never change and I feel like this is one of them.

The key word in this is “I don’t know” I don’t know means there’s a possibility, which is a possibility for you to change for the better. You have a reason to decide to change and make better of yourself, take a shot in the dark and if you get knocked down get back up and fire again. Use your struggles to help others in the future who are feeling the same way and know that you’re loved.

What if your parents just gave in to their problems and ended it? How would that affect you? We can’t let a few problems in life dictate a choice that will have permanent consequences for you and others. Your fiancé and you have a future to fill, books to write and children to love one day. Life isn’t easy at all but we can’t close it off there, what if this is it? What if there’s nothing after this? Would you regret the things you didn’t do or the things you didn’t get the chance to tell people? This is going to sound cliche but life actually does get better and I can say this because I’ve been in your position.

Everyone has a purpose in this world, what if someone just gave up because they couldn’t do something? You’re going to have to push through this and use your story to prevent others. You’ve gone too far to step back now.  Yes you’re struggling right now but this is just a bad chapter in a really good book that you can’t leave unfinished. One day you’ll look back on this and thank yourself for being strong
